chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Faḍl, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh or Abū Jaʿfar, peace be upon him, led us in prayer, and he recited Sūrat al-Fātiḥah and the end of Sūrat al-Māʾidah. Then when he gave salām, he turned toward us and said: Indeed, I only intended to teach you.

key_terms.آخِرِ سُورَةِ الْمَائِدَةِ: the concluding verses of Sūrat al-Māʾidah
key_terms.أُعَلِّمَكُمْ: to teach you, indicating an instructional purpose
key_terms.بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: with Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, the opening chapter recited in prayer

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam عليه السلام recite the end of Sūrat al-Māʾidah in prayer and then say he intended to teach the people?
ai.summary: This hadith describes an Imam, peace be upon him, reciting al-Fātiḥah together with the end of Sūrat al-Māʾidah in prayer, then explaining that he did so in order to teach the people. In the chapter context, it relates to the legal discussion of recitation in obligatory salat and illustrates an instructional action performed for teaching.
